env.name: PLUNK_REDIS_DB
env.generate: case "$BENTO_STACK_KEY" in *-????????) echo $(( 5 + 0x$(printf %s "$BENTO_STACK_KEY" | md5sum | cut -c1-4) % 11 ));; *) echo 2;; esac

env.name: AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID
env.prompt: AWS SES access key (leave default if not using email yet — Plunk's API crashes on boot if this is blank)

env.name: S3_ENDPOINT
env.prompt: S3-compatible endpoint (AWS S3, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, etc. — see docs/reference/plunk-s3.md)

env.name: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
env.prompt: S3 access key (leave default if not using uploads yet)

env.name: S3_PUBLIC_URL
env.prompt: Public URL that serves bucket objects (email recipients load images from here)

env.name: S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE
env.prompt: Force path-style S3 addressing (true for MinIO/most non-AWS providers, false for real AWS S3)

env.name: EMAIL_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND
env.prompt: SES send-rate ceiling (msgs/sec) — check AWS Console > SES > Account dashboard > "Sending statistics" for your account's Maximum send rate, then set this to ~80% of that number. Our IAM policy doesn't grant ses:GetSendQuota, so leaving the default means the worker silently falls back to 14/sec
